Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) is Tortured Until he is Forced to Utter Words of Kufr While his Heart was Content with Imaan

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Muhammad bin Ammaar
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Muhammad bin Ammaar narrates that the Mushrikeen captured Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) and tortured him so brutally that (to save his life) he was eventually forced to blaspheme against Rasulullaah ﷺ and praise the gods of the Mushrikeen. When he came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him what had happened. He replied, "Happenings have been foul indeed, O Rasulullaah ﷺ. The Mushrikeen continued torturing me so much that I was forced to blaspheme against you and praise their gods. "How is the condition of your heart?" asked Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) replied, "I find that my heart is content with Imaan." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "If the Mushrikeen repeat their torture, you may repeat what you said (to save your life)."[^2]

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ammaar narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ met Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) as he was weeping. Wiping the tears from his face, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The Kuffaar captured you and immersed you in water so many times that you were forced to say certain things (words of kufr). Should they do so again, you may say it to them again."

Hadhrat Ameerul Mu'mineen bin Maymoon narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was passing by as the Mushrikeen used open fire to burn Hadhrat Ammaar (RA). Passing his hand over the head of Hadhrat Ammaar (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O fire! Become cool and comfortable for Ammaar as you had become for Ibraheem (AS)." Rasulullaah ﷺ then informed Hadhrat Ammaar (RA) that (he would not die from the torture but that) a group of rebels would martyr him.[^3]
Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat (RA) Endures Difficulties and Hardships
The Incident of Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Imaam Sha'bi narrates that when Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat (RA) once came to the gathering of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) made him sit on his own cushion. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "Besides one man, there is none on the surface of this earth who deserves to occupy this place more than you." "Who is this man, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" asked Hadhrat
Abu Nu'aym in Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.140). Ibn Sa'd has also narrated it in his Tabaqaat (Vol.3 Pg.178).
